races.name: Pennine Brewing Company Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Vinciamo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 51-day break with gelding operation, should benefit from sustained gallop but needs to prove turf effectiveness
runners_data.comment: Too free on stable debut (5f, AW) last month after 11 months off; still capable of better
runners_data.spotlight: Third in a Newbury maiden (5f, good) in April last year on only start for Marcus Tregoning; subsequently gelded and absent for 11 months; third at Newcastle on stable debut in March (5f) but well beaten on Tapeta last time (5f); back after a wind op with tongue-tie on; a possible.

runners_data.name: Forest Phoenix
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with concerning fade pattern in finishes, faces tough tactical assignment against likely honest pace
runners_data.comment: Big prices/well held in three runs; likely to be seen to better effect once handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown modest form over 6f/7f and likely to be one for handicaps.

runners_data.name: Skip To Victory
runners_data.note: Natural front runner making turf debut after three Southwell runs, gets significant weight relief and tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Good efforts over C&D on her last two starts; leading form claims
runners_data.spotlight: All three runs have been over 5f at Southwell, best effort when beaten a head in February; turf debut (half-sister to a Listed turf winner); chance.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Prominent type bouncing back from soft ground disappointment, recent run at Haydock only nine days ago raises freshness questions
runners_data.comment: Second at Doncaster and Ayr but well beaten on soft ground at Haydock yesterday
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing on soft ground at Haydock last week, but comes into the reckoning on his two previous runs when second in a Doncaster novice (6f, good to firm) and in an Ayr maiden (6f, good to firm); speedy and should be as effective at this trip; worth considering.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with ordinary AW form, gets weight relief but tactical setup works against her running style completely
runners_data.comment: Beat one home on her Newcastle debut in December; major improvement required
runners_data.spotlight: Ordinary form in maiden/novice on the AW over 5f/6f and best watched for now.

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Hold-up style 14-race maiden carrying top weight, recent Catterick run four days ago suggests connections optimistic despite poor record
runners_data.comment: Hasn't finished within 10l of the winner in 13 starts
runners_data.spotlight: 14-race maiden who has a very stiff task in this novice event.

races.paceDynamic: Skip To Victory is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start, likely facing minimal early pressure in this small field. Vinciamo and Stoneacre Joe as prominent runners may track close but neither is aggressive enough to challenge the lead early. The pace will be steady rather than fierce, allowing Skip To Victory to control fractions through halfway before the field closes late. This sustainable tempo strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close early, while the hold-up horses face a significant tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Skip To Victory sets uncontested fractions and maintains kick
scenarios.body: The pace leader gets an easy time of it early and has enough left to repel late challengers on turf debut. Prominent racers tracking close also benefit from the tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Vinciamo or Stoneacre Joe sit close and time run perfectly
scenarios.body: The front runner sets it up but gets collared late by a horse with better tactical positioning than the hold-up brigade. Fresh legs from the prominent pack prove decisive in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Drive Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong and tests stamina reserves
scenarios.body: Skip To Victory goes too fast early under pressure and ties up, allowing a staying-on type to pick up the pieces. The honest pace exposes fitness levels across the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold Up Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the front end collapses completely and pace becomes crawling
scenarios.body: The early tempo becomes so slow that closing horses get a genuine chance to unleash finishing kicks. Hold-up horses find the gaps they need in the straight.

watchPoints.text: Skip To Victory could steal this if allowed uncontested lead on turf debut with tactical advantage being decisive
Stoneacre Joe's quick turnaround from Haydock could impact performance despite previous good form on similar going
Forest Phoenix and other hold-up horses face difficult task if Skip To Victory controls tempo from the front
Vinciamo's 51-day absence and turf return could expose fitness levels despite promising earlier form
Aurora's Doublesix running again after four days suggests trainer confidence but 14 defeats tell the story

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: 16-race maiden returning after 130 days off but showed ability in placed efforts at higher levels last season
runners_data.comment: Now 0-16 but this much more realistic than C&D novice she contested on Tuesday
runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden; would have a sound chance on her two seconds at Musselburgh off much higher marks last August/September but didn't progress on the AW in the winter; could go well back on turf after a 130-day break.

runners_data.name: Moretons
runners_data.note: Ex-George Scott runner settling into new yard with fair recent form, though 3lb claimer adds pressure
runners_data.comment: Plenty of chances now but won't mind the return to the AW and looks set to go well again
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-George Scott; has run a couple of fair races for new yard, notably when 2l fifth of seven at Musselburgh in April (5f, good); overall has a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: With Glory
runners_data.note: Best effort came in soft ground last October, yet to prove effectiveness for new connections on good going
runners_data.comment: Two poor efforts for her new yard this spring and isn't obviously fancied
runners_data.spotlight: Best run when second of four in a Musselburgh novice (5f, soft) on final start for Iain Jardine last October; yet to hit top form for new yard (6f/5f), but has been dropped 10lb.

runners_data.name: O Fortuna
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits this scenario perfectly, cheekpieces retained after improved Nottingham effort last time
runners_data.spotlight: Best of his seven runs was on second handicap start when 3.25l fifth of nine at Nottingham last time (5f, good; cheekpieces on for first time and retained); each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Strong puller whose front-running tendencies conflict with prominent style, 34 days since last run
runners_data.comment: Beaten 10l on Sunday's handicap debut at Nottingham (6f; 10-1); hood removed
runners_data.spotlight: Strong-puller; best form when 3.75l third of three in a Newcastle maiden last September; subsequently given wind surgery, but well beaten at Nottingham on handicap debut last month (6f, good; hood tried but now discarded); drop to 5f could suit.

runners_data.name: You Mystify Me
runners_data.note: Unraced running style makes him interesting on handicap debut with solid placed form in maidens
runners_data.comment: Gets the sex allowance under 7lb claimer Lewis Chalkley, which gives her each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: Placed behind a couple of smart sorts on first two runs (5f, good to firm/good), although the overall form didn't amount to a great deal; makes handicap debut after poor run last time (6f, good); worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Flybar
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader returning after 252 days off but low mark of 48 gives her genuine winning chance
runners_data.spotlight: Modest efforts over 6f/7f last term, including in two nurseries, with a visor tried on final start (7f); on a lowly mark, and with her stable gong well, is one to consider on first try at 5f.

runners_data.name: I'm Dan Dare
runners_data.note: Another leader who nearly won last time at Redcar, cheekpieces retained and yard change adds intrigue
runners_data.comment: Just touched off at Redcar ten days ago; a 2lb rise shouldn't prevent another big run
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Adrian Nicholls; best run when beaten a nose at Redcar earlier this month (6f, good; cheekpieces on for first time); has changed yards after a disappointing run last time; one to consider despite the drop in trip.

runners_data.name: Powernap
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tongue-tie fitted, hasn't fired this season but showed promise in nurseries last autumn
runners_data.comment: Has shown little on turf so far; makes AW debut and needs to show improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't run up to her best on her two runs this year, latest on the AW, having shaped with a degree of promise in a couple of nurseries last October; tongue-tie now tried; well drawn.

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 231 days off with hood fitted, plenty to prove after disappointing debut season
runners_data.comment: Finished last in two turf runs for Kevin Ryan; makes stable debut with a point to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten on both runs for Kevin Ryan and no significant improvement after changing yards mid-season; back after a break but plenty to prove, particularly from outside draw.

races.paceDynamic: Flybar and I'm Dan Dare will dispute the early lead in this 5f sprint, with both needing to show pace from the gates. Behind them, a cluster of prominent runners (Havin A Flyer, Moretons, With Glory, Sea Her Excel) will create significant traffic problems entering the final two furlongs as they all seek similar positions. The honest gallop set by the two leaders, combined with the prominent congestion, will create gaps for hold-up horses in the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up merchants who can stay out of trouble and deliver late kicks when the pace-setters tire and the prominent runners get shuffled back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses capitalize
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest and prominent runners get shuffled in traffic 2f out
scenarios.body: The leaders will tire from their early duel while the clustered prominent runners impede each other, creating space for closers to sweep through. O Fortuna, You Mystify Me, and Powernap can exploit the gaps with late runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent position perfect
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent runner can secure the ideal pitch just behind the leaders
scenarios.body: With less traffic than expected, a well-positioned prominent runner can strike at the optimal moment before the hold-up horses wind up. Havin A Flyer or Moretons could capitalize on their experience at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front runner stays
scenarios.trigger: If Flybar or I'm Dan Dare gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear
scenarios.body: The winner could steal a decisive break while the field sorts itself out behind, holding on from a position of strength. I'm Dan Dare's recent near-miss at Redcar suggests he has the gate speed and stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses early
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast and tie up dramatically in the final furlong
scenarios.body: A messy race where the early pace proves unsustainable, allowing any horse with a turn of foot to pick up the pieces late. Even the outsiders could benefit from such a scenario.

watchPoints.text: I'm Dan Dare and Flybar could go too fast early if both are keen to lead, setting up the race for closers
Watch for traffic problems 2f out when Havin A Flyer, Moretons, With Glory and Sea Her Excel converge
You Mystify Me is unraced over this trip and his true running style remains unclear despite prominent rating
O Fortuna retains cheekpieces after his best effort last time and the hold-up style perfectly suits this pace shape
Flybar returns after 252 days off but Hugo Palmer's stable is in good form and her low weight helps

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Unraced but well-bred newcomer whose market position will be crucial given his hold-up style needs the race to develop properly
runners_data.spotlight: Tenth foal; half-brother to four winners at up to 1m2f; dam a 5f Listed winner; interesting newcomer who is worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Grasmere Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed promise on debut but needs a stronger pace than Mr Writer alone is likely to provide
runners_data.spotlight: Gelding by Harry Angel; creditable second of ten in a 7f Newcastle novice on debut (33-1; two market leaders underperformed, but overall form fair); improvement likely; interesting on turf debut.

runners_data.name: Mr Writer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven form advantage who should get favorable pace scenario in this tactical contest
runners_data.comment: Has some potential but needs to settle better if he is to fulfill it
runners_data.spotlight: Quite exposed; sound effort when runner-up off a mark of 77 in a Lingfield turf handicap last time (7f, good to firm); sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Brouhaha
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from lengthy break after wind operation, needs the race to unfold with genuine tempo
runners_data.comment: Unraced for Ed walker; wind surgery/gelded last year; watch the market on this debut
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded and had a wind op before his debut in March when 17l sixth of 11 in a Southwell maiden (28-1; slowly away); that form working out quite well and better expected.

runners_data.name: Pacific Glory
runners_data.note: Moderate hold-up horse whose best chance comes if the race becomes messy or tactical
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form so far (ninth of 11 in a C&D novice last time) and looks more one for handicaps.

runners_data.name: Gardening
runners_data.note: Weak form hold-up runner returning from long absence under claiming jockey, needs everything to fall perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: 13-2 when 17l fifth of six in a Newcastle fillies novice when with Karl Burke last November (6f); bought for 1,000gns three weeks later; plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Writer will lead or sit prominent early with no other confirmed pace angles in this small field. With four hold-up horses (Grasmere Boy, Brouhaha, Pacific Glory, Gardening) likely tracking behind, this sets up as a slow-burn affair where the pace will be modest early before quickening late. Two Commanders as the unknown newcomer could disrupt this if showing early pace, but the pattern points to a tactical race. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed over pure hold-up horses who need a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Writer gets an easy lead and dictates terms throughout
scenarios.body: The exposed handicapper controls the tempo and has enough in hand to resist late challenges from inferior rivals. His proven form at the trip on similar ground gives him a decisive edge when not pressured for the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Newcomer Shows Class
scenarios.trigger: If Two Commanders breaks smartly and shows ability matching his breeding
scenarios.body: The well-bred newcomer from the Bethell yard justifies market support by traveling strongly in behind Mr Writer before showing a turn of foot. His pedigree suggests he should handle the conditions and distance effectively.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes stronger than expected with multiple horses showing speed
scenarios.body: A genuinely-run race allows Grasmere Boy or the improving Brouhaha to use their closing kicks to full effect. The hold-up runners get the strong pace they need to showcase their finishing ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise From Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the market principals underperform and gaps appear for lesser lights
scenarios.body: Pacific Glory or Gardening find significant improvement to capitalize when the favorites fail to fire. The race falls apart tactically allowing a bigger-priced runner to steal through.

watchPoints.text: Mr Writer getting an uncontested lead could make this a procession given his form superiority over these rivals
Two Commanders' market position will reveal stable confidence in this newcomer from a yard that knows when they have one ready
The early positioning of the four hold-up horses could create traffic problems in the straight if they all need to make moves simultaneously
Grasmere Boy showed promise on debut but this slower pace scenario doesn't suit his closing style
Any horse showing unexpected early pace could completely change the complexion of what looks a tactical affair

races.name: Netherfield FC Team Of 1990 Handicap

runners_data.name: Not So Sobers
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over hurdles on latest outing 35 days ago, but limited Flat form suggests jumping is his preferred sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Hurdle/bumper winner (won 2m novice handicap hurdle on latest outing), but perhaps not as effective on the Flat, although was beaten only 1.75l when third of seven off a 2lb higher mark at Chelmsford in February (1m6f); a possible.

runners_data.name: Zephlyn
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer with excellent course form (two wins here last May), but 58 days since last run raises fitness concerns despite previous course success
runners_data.spotlight: In good form on the Flat this time last year, following up 2m win at Newcastle by winning twice over this C&D in May (good/good to firm); not been in top form on AW this year, but better run over hurdles last time; 5lb lower than last Flat win and is one with a chance.

runners_data.name: Fleur De Mer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing retained cheekpieces after sound third last time, but poor turf record (0-10) undermines confidence despite recent AW form
runners_data.spotlight: Not the best of win records (1-26 but 0-10 on turf); only win was over 1m2f on AW back in 2023; sound third at Pontefract with first-time cheekpieces (retained) on reappearance last month (1m4f, good to soft); stays 1m6f but below her best three previous tries at 2m.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Prominent racer gets uncontested lead advantage with blinkers refitted, though poor recent form since November second suggests confidence issues
runners_data.comment: One to watch in the betting following a break but tailed off on AW on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Jim Bolger; close second at Newcastle last November (1m4f) but poor efforts since, including back on turf after a break over 1m4f here last time; blinkers replace cheekpieces; tries this trip for the first time but hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Captain Robert
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with consistent recent AW form in similar trips, but lacks turf experience this year with blinkers applied
runners_data.comment: 1-12; behind Charlie Darling when fourth over C&D 35 days ago; claims
runners_data.spotlight: Has been running creditably on the AW this year (in the frame on last three starts, all over 2m at Southwell); could go well, but below best three previous runs on turf.

runners_data.name: Lillistar
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner just 8 days since last outing, but significantly behind Zephlyn over course and distance previously despite subsequent AW win
runners_data.comment: Not at best Flat or hurdles last month; drop in trip can help but others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Over 6l behind Zephlyn over C&D last May; some fair form since (won over 2m at Wolverhampton in October) but not quite at her best back on turf last twice (over 2m5f and 1m4f); place chance.

races.paceDynamic: Tracker Issue is the sole confirmed front runner in this six-runner field, giving him an uncontested lead over 2m on good ground. With five hold-up horses (Not So Sobers, Zephlyn, Fleur De Mer, Captain Robert, Lillistar) behind him, Tracker Issue can dictate a steady, sustainable gallop without early pressure. The lack of pace competition means the leaders and prominent racers will have a significant tactical advantage, as the hold-up brigade will need to make up considerable ground in the straight. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can track the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tracker Issue gets an easy lead and stays the trip
scenarios.body: The 4yo can control the tempo completely and kick clear when the challengers are still organizing their runs. His prominent style perfectly suits having no pace pressure, despite poor recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow and one hold-up horse has superior class
scenarios.body: Zephlyn or Captain Robert could time their challenge perfectly if Tracker Issue goes too steadily early. Their higher ratings and recent form give them the quality edge in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If Tracker Issue stops quickly and multiple horses finish together
scenarios.body: When the leader fades entering the straight, several hold-up horses could arrive simultaneously in a blanket finish. This favours the most in-form runners who can quicken best from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Shock Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the betting favorites underperform and an outsider strikes
scenarios.body: Not So Sobers or Lillistar could benefit from a truly-run race if their stamina proves superior. The hurdle winner's jumping background might translate to staying power over this extended trip.

watchPoints.text: Tracker Issue could steal this if he gets too easy a lead early, as no other horse will challenge him for pace-setting duties
Watch Zephlyn's market support given his excellent course record but lengthy absence since last run could impact fitness levels
Captain Robert's settling ability is crucial since his hold-up style needs the race to develop into a sprint finish
Check Fleur De Mer's early position as her poor turf record suggests she needs everything to fall perfectly
Monitor if Not So Sobers shows any early keenness given his recent hurdle success might have sharpened his enthusiasm

races.name: Ann Whitehouse Memorial Veterans' Handicap

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in excellent form with three wins this year, 35 days since last run could be ideal freshening up period.
runners_data.spotlight: Has been a superb servant, winning 16 of his 99 starts, including three this year; comfortable scorer at Haydock (6f, good to firm) latest, for which he has gone up 6lb; has won over C&D and looks a player again.

runners_data.name: Wen Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario, though inconsistency remains a concern despite recent Carlisle third.
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time winner on good or slower (placed here over 5f); inconsistent but put a lacklustre effort behind him when third at Carlisle (5f, good) latest; capable of being competitive.

runners_data.name: Evocative Spark
runners_data.note: Course winner in great form with hold-up style perfectly suited to likely strong early gallop from dual pace angle.
runners_data.comment: Won on last three visits to Catterick; still fairly treated off 67 based on historic form.
runners_data.spotlight: Arrives in great form, having won three of his four turf starts this season, two of those here over 7f and the latest over C&D; up another 4lb but looked like he had a bit more up his sleeve last time; big player.

runners_data.name: Mark's Choice
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist making course debut away from favourite Ripon, but confirmed pace-setter will ensure honest tempo.
runners_data.comment: Ten-time course winner who is not ruled back at this track on his second run after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Standing dish at Ripon, where he's recorded ten of his 12 wins; his 71st start is his first here; below par in both starts this season; drops 2lb but perhaps needs further favours from the handicapper to win again.

runners_data.name: Ramon Di Loria
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 65-day break, back to last winning mark but trainer form remains poor at 0/11.
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple AW and turf winner from 5f-7f; back on his last winning turf mark from Ayr 13 months ago (has twice won on AW since); below par latest but not ruled out if able to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Holbache
runners_data.note: Prominent style could benefit if positioned behind early pace battle, though 144 days absence and first-time course visit noted.
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple sprint winner who runs here for the first time; 3lb higher than when last winning at Leicester (6f, good to soft) last September; not badly treated on that form but has yet to produce one of his better efforts following a break.

runners_data.name: Quercus
runners_data.note: Course specialist with leading style, loves this track but has been well below par in both starts since last course win.
runners_data.comment: C&D winner in 2024; two Catterick wins last summer; off since November; new trainer
runners_data.spotlight: Loves it here, with all but one of his eight wins coming over C&D; not ground dependent; has been well below par in both starts since last winning (for Ann Duffield) here last September; not ruled out back here with 7lb claimed but it will need one of his better efforts from this mark.

races.paceDynamic: Mark's Choice and Quercus are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early pace in this seven-runner handicap. Both horses have leading styles and will ensure an honest gallop from the start, with Mark's Choice likely to press forward despite being away from his favoured Ripon. The dual pace angle should create a solid tempo that stretches the field over this straight six furlongs. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can finish from off the pace, as the early leaders may compromise each other.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Mark's Choice and Quercus engage in early battle and compromise each other
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will set up perfectly for the closers who can pick up the pieces in the final furlong. Good Earth, Wen Moon and Evocative Spark all have hold-up styles that suit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner gets loose
scenarios.trigger: If one of Mark's Choice or Quercus gets an uncontested lead while the other falters early
scenarios.body: The loose leader could steal a march and prove difficult to peg back over this sharp track. Mark's Choice or Quercus would benefit from having the race run to suit their natural pace-setting styles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent runners strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ramon Di Loria and Holbache can track the leaders without getting involved in early pace battle
scenarios.body: The prominent pair can sit just behind the speed and time their challenges perfectly when the leaders weaken. Their tracking positions allow them to avoid the early pace pressure while staying close enough to strike.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If both Mark's Choice and Quercus underperform and fail to provide adequate early pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish with no true tempo, potentially suiting any horse that gets a smooth passage. Without genuine pace pressure, form horses like Evocative Spark could benefit from the tactical scenario.

watchPoints.text: Mark's Choice and Quercus both breaking fast and engaging in early speed duel that compromises both leaders.
Good Earth getting too far back in small field as Daniel Muscutt may struggle to make up ground from rear in seven-runner race.
Evocative Spark's position early as hold-up horse will need clear run in final furlong to capitalize on expected pace setup.
Ramon Di Loria's fitness after 65-day layoff combined with Ewan Whillans' poor recent trainer form of 0/11.
Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim on Holbache helping offset the 144-day absence and first-time course conditions.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap

runners_data.name: Mademoiselle Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid 6f turf form including a close second at Nottingham from this mark, but needs to overcome tactical disadvantage
runners_data.spotlight: 5f AW winner who has been placed over 5f and 6f on turf; beaten just 1l from the same mark at Nottingham (6f, good) but well below that level when back there over 5f (good) latest; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who has struggled on turf but drops to workable mark with cheekpieces returning after 11-day break
runners_data.comment: Held in two runs back in handicaps; 3lb lower but she's looking exposed now
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 and a filly whose better efforts were both on AW surfaces; slipping to a workable mark and headgear again being tried (previously wore blinkers once but was last of five); need to see more.

runners_data.name: Agric Ranger
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner with ideal tactical position, though his initial handicap mark looks potentially harsh after three qualifying runs
runners_data.spotlight: The best of his three qualifying efforts (all last month) came on debut at Pontefract (6f, good to soft); initial mark looks a bit stiff based on what he's produced but no surprise if he improves now entering handicaps.

runners_data.name: Populus
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse adding cheekpieces after 86-day break, showed glimpses of ability but faces stiff task from poor draw
runners_data.spotlight: Showed minor ability in one of her qualifying starts (6f, AW) but was never involved on her handicap debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) latest; cheekpieces go on; more needed.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but recent Ripon second over 6f on good ground suggests she's finding form at the right time
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7; better efforts have both been over 6f (good and good to soft), including at Ripon latest, when she raced prominently and stuck on well when the winner had asserted; up 2lb and looks a player.

runners_data.name: Mereside Spark
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best form was last September, concerning that she bled from nose on latest start 42 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort to date was at Beverley (5f, soft) last September but has been well below that level in two starts since (vet reported she bled from the nose latest); others preferred.

races.paceDynamic: Agric Ranger is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the rail, likely getting an uncontested lead in this small field. With five hold-up horses behind him, there's minimal early pace pressure, allowing Agric Ranger to control fractions and potentially steal a march. The lack of prominent racers means the hold-up brigade must time their moves perfectly from off the pace. This race shape heavily favours front runners and any horse that can sit close to the pace, as the hold-up horses face a tactical disadvantage with limited early speed to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Agric Ranger gets soft fractions and isn't caught napping
scenarios.body: He controls the tempo completely and has enough left to repel late challenges from horses giving him too much start. The lack of pace pressure plays directly into his hands.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses time their runs perfectly despite the lack of pace
scenarios.body: One of the better-rated hold-up horses overcomes the tactical disadvantage through superior class. Mademoiselle Belle or Battenburg Belle could benefit from their recent good form over the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Agric Ranger goes too fast early trying to make all
scenarios.body: The front runner cracks in the final furlong after overexerting, allowing the closers to swamp him late. This requires Agric Ranger to misjudge the fractions significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Ambush
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders underperform and conditions suit an improver
scenarios.body: One of the lesser-fancied runners like Populus or Mereside Spark finds significant improvement with headgear changes. This requires multiple favorites to disappoint simultaneously.

races.paceDynamic: La Tosca will lead uncontested from the start, with Mohaasset and Favourite Friend likely to track in prominent positions early. The five hold-up horses (Gemical, Star Of Emerald, Evergreen Emerald, Red Rifle) will settle behind this modest pace. La Tosca can dictate comfortable fractions without pressure, then kick clear in the straight while the closers struggle to make up ground on good turf at this trip. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: La Tosca Leads Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If La Tosca maintains her lead without serious pressure through halfway
scenarios.body: She can dictate ideal fractions and has enough in reserve to resist late challenges. The hold-up brigade will find the task too difficult against an uncontested leader on this course.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mohaasset or Favourite Friend can improve significantly and challenge La Tosca turning in
scenarios.body: The pace-tracking horses can strike while La Tosca weakens, benefiting from their forward position. Hold-up horses still face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple horses vying for the lead
scenarios.body: This creates the perfect setup for Gemical or Red Rifle to unleash late runs. The pace-setters will collapse, opening the door for patient tactics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset Winner
scenarios.trigger: If multiple front-runners engage in an early speed duel that compromises all pace factors
scenarios.body: Star Of Emerald or Evergreen Emerald could benefit from a completely collapsed pace scenario. This requires significant pace pressure that seems unlikely given the small field.
